topics.topic: Atomic ordering of concurrent requests that mutate one owner session
questions: When concurrent owner requests show confirmation steps or otherwise change the same session state, in what order are they applied and which pending confirmation survives?
If upload and confirmation overlap in one owner session, which file state does confirmation observe and may it commit using the replaced file?
What atomic ordering guarantees that two concurrent submissions carrying the same pending value cannot both pass the one-time check?

quotes:
A session holds at most one: showing a confirmation step
   replaces the one pending (M11).

A submission
   carries it when it passes the owner session and CSRF checks (A04 rule 6,
   stage 1) and gives a value equal to the pending one; from there on,
   whatever the answer — a binding to another action or input included — the
   pending value is used up.

The uploaded file is kept in the owner session that uploaded it, never in
   the store, until the import is accepted, another file is uploaded in that
   session, or the session ends (M11); then it is dropped.
judgement.divergence: One implementation serialises mutations of an owner session, so exactly one concurrent confirmation survives or consumes the value and a confirmation sees either the old or new uploaded file; another performs separate unsynchronised checks and updates, allowing both submissions to pass or confirmation to use a file concurrently replaced, which the owner and Registry store observe.
judgement.why: The texts require replacement and one-time use but do not order or atomically combine concurrent mutations of the same owner session.

topics.topic: Canonical encoding and digest for confirmation-bound inputs
questions: Which digest algorithm, value encoding, normalization and fixed field order define equality of confirmation-bound inputs?
How are confirmation-bound inputs converted into bytes and digested so showing and submitting the same inputs always compare identically?
What exact canonical encoding, field order, digest algorithm, and treatment of absent versus blank values are used to calculate the confirmation binding?

quotes:
kept as a digest of those values in a fixed order, never
   as the values themselves; a submission's inputs are bound when their digest
   equals it.
judgement.why: The canonical byte encoding, field order, digest algorithm and representation of absent values are encoding and contract details owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Cryptographic algorithm, encoding, key handling, and authenticated format for backups
questions: Which authenticated-encryption scheme, nonce handling, key derivation, file format and authentication coverage—including whether the clear metadata is authenticated—define a valid backup?
What cryptographic format must every release use to encrypt, authenticate, identify, and later restore a backup?
Which authenticated-encryption algorithm, nonce generation, file format, key interpretation or derivation, and metadata authentication rules define a valid encrypted backup?
Are the cleartext metadata authenticated by the encrypted backup, and what exact key-digest algorithm and domain separation are used?

judgement.why: This is the same backup authenticated-encryption and envelope-format question already assigned to State 6, and the cited texts have not changed.

precedent.topic: Authenticated-encryption format and authenticated metadata for backups
quotes: Each backup is encrypted with the backup key the configuration holds at its making (A17).
A backup cannot be read without the key it was made with.
precedent.why: The algorithm, nonce, authenticated envelope, key identifier and cryptographic-version representation are encoding and file-format contract details owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Definition and durable storage of the last backup-run result
questions: Where is the last-run result kept, and after a restart does 'last run' mean the last attempted run before the restart or only a run in the current process?
Is the last-run result durable across restarts, and how is ‘last run’ determined when the latest attempt produced no kept backup?
What counts as a failed run, and where is that status kept so it survives a restart without becoming an undeclared store record or configuration item?

quotes:
The owner interface shows the instant of the
   newest kept backup and whether the last run failed, so the owner sees when
   a backup holds the import (A16 rule 10).

A backup that fails the
   check is deleted and counts as failed.

A backup or a deletion that fails leaves no partial file, writes a
   diagnostic that names the failure and no value (A17), and is tried again at
   the next run; Registry keeps serving.
judgement.divergence: One implementation persists the outcome of every attempted run and shows a pre-restart failure until a later run succeeds; another keeps the outcome only in process memory and shows no failure after restart, which the owner notices in the backup-status view.
judgement.why: The interface must report the last failure, but the texts do not define the status's persistence or how a failed attempt with no kept backup remains the last run.

topics.topic: Post-import backup behavior when that UTC day already has a checked backup
questions: If the day's daily backup already succeeded before an import, is a second post-import backup made, is the earlier backup replaced, or is the import-triggered run skipped?
What happens when an import is accepted after a checked daily backup already exists for that UTC day?
If a checked daily backup already exists for that UTC day, must the post-import run create a second backup, replace the day's backup, or make no backup until the next day?
Does “at most one backup” include the post-import run when an earlier backup already exists that day, or is the post-import run an exception allowed to create a second backup?

quotes:
The import answers once its transaction commits; right after it
   Registry makes a backup run outside the daily schedule (A18), so the import
   reaches a checked backup as soon as it can, and the owner interface shows
   when it has (A18 rule 1); a failed run is retried at the next run, and the import stays
   accepted.

Besides the run after an accepted
   import (A16), which counts as that day's backup, at most one backup is
   made per UTC day, the kept backups themselves saying which days have one,
   and runs never overlap.
judgement.why: A16 requires a run immediately after import, while A18 permits at most one backup that day and supplies no exception when an earlier daily backup already exists.

topics.topic: Validation and handling of malformed records outside selectable or picked projects
questions: What happens at upload when a syntactically readable project record lacks an id or status, so it cannot be displayed or selected, but is not one of the two stated whole-upload refusal cases?
Which malformed records and conflicts outside the picked projects must be detected or shown?
Besides duplicate project ids and an unreadable envelope, may arbitrary malformed room, pointer, status, instant, or reference data belonging only to unpicked projects remain in an accepted file?

quotes:
Registry
   reads it as data (A19) and answers, without changing anything, each
   project the file holds with its id and status.

Registry checks what the picks bring in — each picked project with the
   rooms and pointers that name it and the v1 value it names — and nothing
   else of the file; a room or pointer naming another project belongs to that
   project: records only of projects the owner did not pick are neither checked,
   shown as conflicts nor imported, and take no part in the duplicate-id
   check.

A file that cannot be read as the format States 5 and 6 declare,
   or that holds two project records with one id, is refused whole at
   upload, before anything is picked.
judgement.divergence: One implementation treats a syntactically readable project lacking an id or status as an unreadable file and refuses the upload; another retains or ignores that malformed unselectable record and permits selected valid projects to be imported, which the owner notices at upload and confirmation.
judgement.why: The rules exempt unpicked records from validation but do not say how a malformed project that cannot be displayed or picked is classified.

topics.topic: Whether an empty audit erasure mints and records a confirmation id
questions: When an accepted audit erasure removes no old entry, is a confirmation id minted?
Does an accepted audit erasure that removes no old entry mint and record a confirmation id?
Does an accepted audit erasure that removes no entry mint a confirmation id, as A15 rule 6 requires, or mint none under A14 rule 5?

quotes:
A confirmation id is minted only for an accepted, confirmed action that
   changes state, and is written into its entry (and, for the import, into the
   migration closure); a confirmed action that changes nothing mints none.

An erasure that removes no entry still writes its own entry naming the
   date, with its confirmation id: R0-66 makes the erasure leave an entry of
   its own, whatever it removed.
judgement.why: A14 forbids minting a confirmation id for a no-change action, while A15 requires that id for an audit erasure that removes nothing.

topics.topic: Audit-entry eligibility for an audit erasure that removes nothing
questions: Does an accepted erasure of old audit entries that removes no prior entry satisfy A14's entry-writing rule despite not changing pre-existing state?

Is an audit erasure that removes no old entry formally a state-changing action because it appends its own entry, or is it a no-op exception to the requirement that only state-changing actions write entries?

quotes:
An accepted action that changes nothing (A03 rule 4, A05) writes no entry,
   but for the erasure of old audit entries (A15 rule 6).

It is the one accepted action that writes an
   entry without changing other state (A14 rule 3).
judgement.why: The texts expressly make an empty audit erasure the sole no-change exception that still writes an entry.

topics.topic: How Registry identifies temporary files it is authorized to delete
questions: Exactly which files is Registry authorized to classify and delete as its temporary backup or check files?
How does Registry identify its own temporary files so it does not remove unrelated files in the configured backup location?

quotes:
A backup and its check file are
   written under temporary names in the backup location and become a kept
   backup only when complete; at every start and every run Registry first
   removes every temporary file left there.
judgement.divergence: One implementation deletes only files matching a Registry-owned temporary-name convention; another classifies broader incomplete or unknown files as temporary and deletes them, which the owner notices if unrelated files in the configured backup location disappear.
judgement.why: The deletion rule does not define the boundary that distinguishes Registry's temporary files from other files.

topics.topic: Representation of an audit-erasure cutoff in recovery records
questions: For an audit-erasure action, which touches neither a customer nor a project, where is the cutoff date needed to repeat the erasure after restore recorded, and is it distinct from the action's date?
How does that record represent an erasure of old audit entries, which touches neither a customer nor a project but must preserve the cutoff date for restoration?

quotes:
What the owner repeats after a restore — erasures,
restrictions, ends of a relationship, the latest date audit entries were
erased by — follows the owner's record of the retention review (R0-60): a
governance document, outside this case (Explicit exclusions), naming each
action by its date, kind and the `customer_ref` or `project_id` it touched,
with no personal value.
judgement.why: The representation of the external governance document is a note outside Registry's rules and belongs to State 7.

topics.topic: Request-id validity, format, length, entropy, and collision-resistance requirements
questions: Is an empty or whitespace-only request id considered present, and what format, length or entropy limits must request ids satisfy?
What format and collision-resistance requirement must owner-interface and Kernel request-id generators meet, since Registry cannot verify that a reused value represents the same intended create?

quotes:
'Create a project', 'record a customer', 'add a room' and 'publish an
   artifact pointer' each carry a request id: an opaque value the caller
   makes, unique for every create it means as new.
A create without a request id is refused.
judgement.divergence: One implementation accepts an empty or whitespace-only request id as an opaque present value and deduplicates all uses of it; another refuses it as missing, which callers notice, while generators with different collision guarantees can also cause unintended replay refusals.
judgement.why: The rules make presence and uniqueness behaviorally significant but do not define whether blank values are present or impose any verifiable generation requirement.

topics.topic: Whether a mismatched submission clears an already expired confirmation
questions: Does a mismatched submission clear a pending confirmation that has already expired?
When the pending confirmation is expired but the submission gives a different value, is the expired pending confirmation cleared or left in place?

quotes:
It is valid only in that session, while
   less than 10 minutes have passed since it was shown — an expired one is
   refused and cleared — and is used up by the first submission that carries it, whatever
   its answer; a refused submission needs the step shown again.

A submission refused before those checks, or
   giving another value, is refused and leaves the pending value as it was.
judgement.why: For a mismatched submission against an expired pending value, one rule requires clearing the expired value while the other requires leaving it unchanged.

topics.topic: Whether import and its post-import backup are allowed during owner-only recovery
questions: May the owner repeat a lost import while the restored instance is in owner-only mode, and if so does the mandatory post-import backup run despite the owner-only prohibition?
If the owner repeats the import during the mandatory owner-only recovery phase, does its special post-import backup run, and must reconciliation finish before that import?

quotes:
A store lost before a checked backup holds the import loses the import
with it, and the import may then be made again: the owner keeps the export file
and the picks, names and aliases given in the import until a checked backup
holds the import, and retires the VPS instance only then (R0-79).

The import answers once its transaction commits; right after it
   Registry makes a backup run outside the daily schedule (A18), so the import
   reaches a checked backup as soon as it can, and the owner interface shows
   when it has (A18 rule 1); a failed run is retried at the next run, and the import stays
   accepted.

An owner-only start makes no backup run, so no backup
   holds the store before this is done.
judgement.divergence: One implementation permits the repeated import during owner-only recovery and runs its special immediate backup; another suppresses every backup in owner-only mode or postpones the import until recovery reconciliation and a token-enabled restart, which the owner notices and which changes when the restored import becomes protected.
judgement.why: The texts permit repeating the lost import and mandate its immediate backup but do not order it relative to reconciliation or resolve the owner-only prohibition on backup runs.

topics.topic: Atomic ordering of import against concurrent ordinary writes and identity conflicts
questions: How is an import ordered against concurrent ordinary creates or writes that could introduce an id conflict after the confirmation check but before the import commits?

topics.topic: Concurrency rule for two changes based on the same project revision
questions: Can two concurrent changing actions that both state the same current revision both be accepted, or must exactly one win and the other be stale?

topics.topic: Distinguishing a first installation from a missing or lost production store
questions: How does Registry distinguish an intentional first installation from a lost, deleted or wrongly configured production store that must be restored under R0-89?

topics.topic: Distinguishing intentional owner-only startup from accidentally missing service tokens
questions: How does Registry distinguish an intentional owner-only start from an accidentally missing set of all four service tokens?

topics.topic: Encoding and byte-length rules for textual secrets
questions: How is byte length measured for textual configuration values, and are secrets decoded from a required encoding before the length and equality checks?

topics.topic: Equality and normalization rules for grouping v1 customer references
questions: What equality determines that two v1 customer-reference values are distinct, including whitespace, case, Unicode normalization, and values that are blank?

topics.topic: Evidence that a checked backup contains an accepted import
questions: What exact evidence proves that a checked backup contains the accepted import, especially if its audit entry has been erased: closure presence in the checked copy, sequence comparison, backup instant, or another marker?

topics.topic: Exact configuration namespace and treatment of unknown host settings
questions: What exact namespace is Registry's configuration, and which extra host environment variables or configuration-file keys count as unknown items that must stop startup?

topics.topic: Exact digest used to identify an import file
questions: What exact digest identifies an import file in the mapping, confirmation, closure, and audit entry?

topics.topic: Exact scope and attributes of the owner-session cookie
questions: Which exact cookie scope and attributes implement “Registry's own origin,” given that cookies are not scoped by port and the interface may also be reached locally without HTTPS?

topics.topic: Fate of uploaded files in other owner sessions after an import is accepted
questions: When one session accepts the import, are uploaded files in every other owner session dropped or do they remain until those sessions end?

topics.topic: Handling collisions of Registry-generated identities or values
questions: Must Registry detect a generated-value collision and retry, or may it overwrite, reuse, or refuse?
On a collision of a Registry-minted identity with an existing record, must Registry retry generation, refuse atomically, or surface an internal failure?

topics.topic: Handling session-bound state created by an in-flight request after sign-out
questions: If that completing request would create or replace session-bound state such as a confirmation or uploaded file after a concurrent sign-out has ended the session, is that state discarded, recreated, or allowed to survive?

topics.topic: Imported record kinds and references subject to room referential checks
questions: Which imported record kinds are permitted or required to name a room, and which exact references must be checked, since the stated Room and ArtifactPointer models name projects but no listed imported model names a room?

topics.topic: Instant at which today is fixed for an audit-erasure cutoff
questions: For a request crossing UTC midnight, at what instant is “today” fixed: arrival, confirmation validation, transaction start, or commit?

topics.topic: Meaning of latest cutoff when multiple audit erasures have occurred
questions: Does “latest date” mean the greatest cutoff date ever supplied, or the cutoff supplied by the most recently performed erasure action?

topics.topic: Ordering of backup cleanup, creation, verification, publication, and retention deletion
questions: Does retention deletion happen before or after temporary cleanup, creation, verification, and publication of the new backup?

topics.topic: Permitted persistent side effects of a failed startup
questions: Must all non-mutating checks pass before Registry creates a store or probe file, and what state may a failed start leave behind?

topics.topic: Required behavior when removal of a temporary or partial backup file fails
questions: When removal of an existing temporary or partial file fails, may that file remain, or must Registry somehow guarantee that no partial file remains?

topics.topic: Timing-resistance requirements for session identity lookup
questions: Does constant-time comparison apply only after locating a session, or must lookup of the cookie's session identity itself avoid data-dependent comparison and timing?

topics.topic: Validation-stage classification of project session membership
questions: Is “project not in the session's set” exclusively a stage-2 authorization check, or is it also a stage-6 lifecycle check?

topics.topic: Whether a refused or invalid form submission retains its request id
questions: After a refused submission or validation error, does the re-rendered form retain the same request id or mint a new one?

topics.topic: Whether archived-project refusal applies to replaying the project's own create
questions: Does the archived-project refusal in the formal invariant apply only to room and pointer creates, or also to replaying the project's own create?

topics.topic: Whether displaying a confirmation step requires CSRF protection
questions: Because showing a confirmation step changes the session by replacing its pending value, must the request that shows the step itself pass CSRF protection?

topics.topic: Whether one operation uses a single fixed value of now
questions: Is one value of `now` fixed for all time-dependent checks and recorded instants in an operation, or may each check and write observe a different time?

topics.topic: Whether recovery material retains all customer-mapping decisions needed to repeat an import
questions: Does the retained recovery material also have to include every Customer mapping input required by A16—kind and whether the v1 value is the tax id—or must the owner decide those again after a restore?
